business: TODO, a body-worn camera with a caregiver app: live video from the wearer, two-way voice, SOS and GPS
by_segment: Adult child caring for a parent with dementia, living nearby or long-distance
Parent of a child with autism or intellectual disability (wanders or is non-verbal)
Spouse or relative of an adult with a disability who wants independence with a safety net
why_not: I'd take the idea seriously, because wandering is the thing that keeps me up at night. But I've never heard of TODO, and this goes on my son's body and into a phone I rely on, so I'm not paying $249 plus a monthly plan for a brand I can't check. I'd need to see real families using it before I'd even consider ordering.

I already pay for AngelSense and it has never failed me on GPS or the SOS button. A video camera sounds nice, but I need to know it will actually connect when Mom is confused and wandering two hours away, and I can't find out from a flyer. I'm not paying $249 plus another $20 a month on a promise.
I already have an AirTag and it does the 'where is he' part for almost nothing. $249 plus $20 a month for video I'd rarely open is a lot to pay for something I'm not sure we'd use every day.

I want this for my mom and my son, and the live video and GPS would give me some peace of mind. But another $19.99 a month on top of everything else, plus $249 up front, is a lot when I already pay for care and gas for the two-hour drive. I would not buy it on an ad. I would go read the support groups first.

My mom is early-stage and still herself, and a camera on her chest that I can open whenever I want feels like watching her, not caring for her. I would rather she have a say in it, and an AirTag in her purse already tells me where she is for a fraction of the cost.

A live camera on my mom feels like watching her every minute, and she would hate it, even with privacy mode. I would also be recording strangers and other people's kids in the background, which I am not comfortable with.
why_yes: After the wandering scare I'm not waiting around for a perfect product. Live video and GPS on him would let me find him fast, and $249 is less than one night of a home-care aide.

After the wandering scare and the police call I cannot keep relying on luck, so a device that tells me where my child is and lets me talk to them is worth the $249 to me. Twenty dollars a month hurts, but less than another night of not knowing.
flip: A free trial or a month-to-month option with no monthly plan required, plus proof that the live video and SOS alert really work from a wandering-prone wearer's device without a long setup.
If she could understand it and agree to it, the camera only switched on when she pressed the SOS button, and a doctor or dementia specialist told me it helps her and does not upset her.
Independent reviews or a parent I know who has used it for a few months with real reliability, plus a clear return policy so I'm not locked in.
A GPS-only mode with no camera, with wandering alerts and a clear rule that video is never on unless a caregiver is responding to an SOS.
A free or refundable trial where I can test a live video call with Mom from two hours away, with a clear answer on what happens when the signal is weak.
A clear written policy showing video is only viewed when there is a real alert, plus a setup I could finish in under ten minutes with no tech help.
Honest reviews from other parents of wandering children showing the GPS and SOS working in a real incident, plus a trial period with a full refund if the device does not do what it says.
Independent reviews from caregivers who have used it for months, showing the battery lasts a full day with live video on and the device survives a dementia patient pulling at it.
A real owner in a caregiver group telling me it connected reliably during a wandering episode, or a free or refundable trial I can run on mum before I commit.
Other caregivers in my Facebook groups and Reddit threads reporting that it works reliably for a wanderer, plus a month-to-month option where I can cancel the plan at any time.
Caregiver groups and independent reviews showing it has actually found a wandering loved one quickly, plus a clear way to switch the camera off that keeps the GPS and SOS working.
Dementia caregivers in the support groups posting that it stays on, the GPS holds up in her neighbourhood, and there is a real return policy if it doesn't work.
A free trial or money-back window where I can test the GPS and SOS alerts in real conditions, plus clear written limits on who can view the live video and when it is recorded.
A free trial or a money-back window where I can test live video and SOS on Dad's own walks, plus a clear answer on how it works where cell coverage is weak.
A clear side-by-side showing it does what my current tracker does for less money, or a trial month where I can cancel with no device lock-in.
A trial I could return for a full refund if he won't keep it on, plus proof it works on a kid who takes things off.
Independent reviews or a caregiver I know personally who has used it for months without a failure, plus a trial period where I can return it for a full refund.
A free trial or a month-to-month plan I could cancel, plus proof from other parents of autistic kids that the live view actually helped them find a wandering child quickly.
